speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your vision issues, can you tell me if the black spots are stationary or if they seem to float around when you move your eyes? Also, have you noticed any pain in the eye or a sudden increase in these spots?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of AIDS, Kaposi's sarcoma, and previous fungal infections, I need to check your current immune status and look for signs of opportunistic infections like CMV retinitis or Toxoplasmosis. I will order some tests to guide my next questions.

The fundoscopic findings of granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages, combined with a critically low CD4 count, are classic for CMV retinitis. I will now confirm the diagnosis with specific imaging.

text:
The clinical picture is definitive: a patient with advanced AIDS (CD4 < 50) presenting with painless vision loss and classic fundoscopic findings of hemorrhages and granular opacities ("pizza pie" retinopathy). These are pathognomonic for Cytomegalovirus retinitis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: CMV Retinitis
